person: Devon Clarke is the 26-year-old finance manager of a twenty-person community kitchen, eight months into the job after leaving an audit team. His predecessor left a binder and a spreadsheet with tabs called FINAL and FINAL2. It is the week after the quarter closed, the audit is four months away, and the executive director has told the board everything is in order. He has to book the restricted-fund releases and file the funder reports himself for the first time, and he wants to understand each step well enough to explain it to his director in one paragraph.
stated_up_front: Hi Athena, it's Friday 9 October and I need to work out which of our restricted funds can be released this quarter and book them, then report the releases to the funders who ask. I'm fairly new at this, so please walk me through what you'd change before anything gets booked or sent.

facts.truth: 23,200 dollars for a walk-in cooler, placed in service 15 September 2026; he believes it can be released.
15,000 dollars, originally available 1 January 2027; he remembers a mailed amendment signed in September moving it earlier, to 1 October 2026.
10,000 dollars for meals; he has 6,300 dollars of food and packaging entries coded to it, and the rest is wages and a gala table he is unsure about.
Roughly 9,400 dollars of allowed costs have been incurred and not yet recognised in a prior release.
Two new donors gave cash totalling 5,700 dollars toward the match; they had not given before.
Ordered with a 4,000 dollar deposit; delivery expected around 20 November, so he assumes it is not ready for release.
45,000 dollar grant that pays out in full at 150 participants; 104 served so far.
A release was already reported to a funder on 3 September; he does not want it sent twice.
A 40,000 dollar board-designated operating reserve and a 50,000 dollar endowment held in perpetuity; he knows neither is a donor-restricted release.
A consultant offered services at 2,400 dollars a quarter; the board has not voted, so he wants no reply committing to it.

unknowns: Whether the gift whose date was moved later by an amendment is still unavailable on its new date.
Which funders' agreements actually require a release report and which do not.
Whether the cooking-classes gift of 6,500 dollars, spent on instructor stipends, is excluded by the donor's terms.
Whether the family's memorial gift needs any report to the donor.
